title: New Rule 10 - English Only Posts and Comments
author: fisj
selftext:
Posts and Comments must be in English, and we've added this as rule 10. We avoided doing this for a while (some of us speak languages other than English too). The reason we're doing this now, is to help moderation. The sub post and comment volume means mods need to scan a lot of things quickly. The feeling is we can't do this trying to translate comments and posts, while also being uncertain the auto translation meaning wasn't mangled.

  
Its not an unreasonable ask for posters and commenters to use translation tools themselves and check the meaning is clear.

comments.author: je386
comments.body: But why? The reddit translate is not worse than others and if you use reddit translate or the redditor used another translation tool, in both cased nuances may be lost or misleading. Even if someone writes in english by himself, but it is not the first language, errors may occur.

replies.author: Warsel77
replies.body: What is the argument for the moderators (who do this for free) to have to do the extra work rather than the person posting?

comments.author: spixt
comments.body:
This is a completely ridiculous rule.  This is an AI sub, we should all be smart enough to actually know how to configure our browsers to automatically translate everything to English.  If we don't trust the AI to translate what we read then we shouldn't trust it to make games.

I have loved how open this sub has been to other languages and it's been awesome seeing people from China, Korea, Germany, France, Spain etc etc all taking part in conversations.   Every now and then I turn off the auto translate and just find it so wholesome seeing completely different languages all responding to each other. It's one of the reasons I thought this sub was more as a whole more ethical and more welcoming than the "anti ai" subs that have strict English-only rules.

\*sigh\*

replies.author: Livid_Shallot5701
replies.body:
I completely do not agree with you. 

The reason was clearly stated: being able to moderate reasonably well. 

This is a FREE sub, and it's not a random demand.

replies.author: meowyih
replies.body: So, if someone says "my post does not break the rule, it's Reddit's translator's problem!" How you plan to handle such kind of argument? Hire a professional translator? :p

replies.author: meowyih
replies.body: One more example, in my language, calling someone 'G8' is a person attack and need to ve banned. But ypu can see it means nothing if I translate to English, right? :-D

replies.author: Warsel77
replies.body:
>we should all be smart enough to actually know how to configure our browsers to automatically translate everything to English. 

Disagree. We should also all be smart enough to use the same category of tools to translate our post into English rather than place the burden on the Mods.

replies.author: TMiyoshi
replies.body:
Why can't the original poster do that? 

If anything, THEY should translate to English, and verify that it actually means what they meant. Or is that too much to ask of a modern AI user?

comments.body:
Meh, Reddit supports auto translations now. Silly rule  
IMO

replies.author: Zenity07

There's browser translation tools of course, but those aren't frictionless especially if you need to quickly scan a page with posts written in multiple languages.
